assessment: A thin, conviction-light regime. The surviving pair is two high-beta Layer-1 tokens with overlapping product narratives, which is consistent with the rejection pattern: when sector-level narratives decouple even briefly, statistical cointegration across most alt pairs breaks down, while within-sector pairs tied by shared factor exposure can still hold together. Cost-aware entry/exit bands will be wide because the 20h half-life forces slow OU mean-reversion and the modest 60 mean-crossing count sits near the floor.
opportunity_set: A single pair, AVAX/SOL, with a tight positive beta of +0.50 indicating a near 2:1 notional ratio for a market-neutral book. The economic rationale is shared Layer-1 / smart-contract-platform exposure: the two assets tend to move together on sector beta, and residual deviations should be noise around that common factor rather than fundamental drift. The Hurst of 0.40 confirms anti-persistence (more mean-reverting than random walk), the 20h half-life is intraday-to-daily and therefore capturable by the cost-aware bands, and the ADF p-value of 0.0001 gives strong stationarity evidence on the full sample. The 60 mean crossings, while acceptable, is near the floor and is the weakest supporting signal. The pair should be sized modestly and the bands should respect the slow reversion so we are not paying fees into a half-life we cannot outpace.
risks: Concentration risk on a single cointegration bet. The tradeable set carries (1) regime-break risk - if the Layer-1 narrative diverges (e.g., one chain ships a catalyst the other does not, or funding rates on perps decouple), the residual can drift persistently rather than revert, and the slow 20h half-life means losses compound before the next OU half-cycle; (2) liquidity/execution risk - both legs are liquid perp books but the cost-aware bands must be wide enough to absorb fees plus slippage on a slow-reverting spread, otherwise the edge is consumed by round-trip costs; (3) false-discovery risk that the one survivor is a lucky artifact of a 13-pair screen, and the rejection pattern (especially 9 split-half cointegration failures) suggests the broader market is not actually providing a robust statistical edge today - we are trading one pair because one passed, not because the regime is broadly mean-reverting.
adaptation: Universe has contracted sharply versus the previous refit. Previously the agent carried AVAX/SOL as an active pair and it has survived today, so the core exposure is unchanged, but the rest of the previous book has been pruned by the gates - likely candidates that were borderline on split-half cointegration or beta stability have failed today's re-test, which is consistent with a regime where cointegration is fragile. Net effect: the agent is running a single-pair book today rather than a diversified basket. This is not a loosening of thresholds and not an attempt to manufacture trades; it is the gates correctly refusing to fund pairs that are not genuinely cointegrated right now. Operationally the agent should treat this as a low-convexity day: size the surviving pair conservatively, keep bands wide, and expect that a regime shift (either re-coupling of the broader alt complex or further decoupling) will be needed before the opportunity set expands again.
